title: Local re-arm integrity: no latch set without an observed local re-arm
requirement_and_acceptance_criterion: The hardware traction latch cannot set without a physical local REARM press, observed by the firmware. (a) Set stage: the K1 coil node is on the board; the set pulse needs the closing edge of the REARM set contact AND the level of the aux contact, and C_SET is charged only from a closed chain and emptied when it opens, so re-arm needs the chain closed continuously for about 1-2 s (hardware; calculated, tau 2.2 s). (b) Firmware accepts a rise of HW_LATCH_RB only within 150 ms (electronics F4) / 250 ms (firmware, ICD) of a debounced REARM edge on both contacts, with every element CLOSED; otherwise fatal LATCH_NO_REARM / LATCH_UNEXPLAINED, permit withdrawn. (c) K1 weld detection: LATCH_NC_RB low with HW_LATCH_RB low for > 30 ms, or LATCH_RUN_RB high without a set pulse, gives fatal K1_WELD; HW_LATCH_RB high with LATCH_RUN_RB low gives RUN_SHORT; REARM_BTN and REARM_SET_RB disagreeing by more than 200 ms gives REARM_DISCREPANCY; REARM held more than 2 s is refused. (d) Hardware barrier behind K1: second diverse hold element U_HOLD, set only by the set pulse, keeps RUN_12V off if K1 is welded. Simulated (emulator aligned with the netlist): welded seal-in, K1_SET short and RUN_12V short each give 0 DRIVE accepted and 0 mm travel. A welded K1 is not seen by the brake test itself; it shows when the permit returns. Follow-up review (IB-70, simulated): a W-018 crush that arms the robot leaves the aux line high and the latch stays set because rrch_rearm_blocked returns false while latched; a REARM contact still closed 2 s after a latch rise should withdraw ARM_PERMIT (requested, not applied). Evidence class: simulated and tool-checked; nothing measured.

title: Re-arm availability: an operator who follows rearm_ready can arm, and a refused re-arm is reported
accountable_role: Chassis electronics + chassis firmware + robot software
requirement_and_acceptance_criterion: A legitimate local re-arm succeeds when the operator presses after the REARM lamp says ready, and every refusal is reported with its reason. Follow-up review (simulated on a patched emulator copy): the set stage needs C_SET of at least 9.0 V at 23 C (about 9.9 V for a 50 C coil; table T11, calculated) but rearm_ready comes after 2 s of closed chain, when C_SET holds about 60 % (7.4-7.6 V from a 12.8-13.0 V pack); the press is refused, each press empties C_SET, and pressing every 0.9 s never armed in 8 s; nothing reports the refusal; the emulator hides it by using a 7.5 V threshold. The needed wait is about 2.9 s from a 12.8 V pack and 3.6 s for a 50 C coil, longer at low battery. Requested changes (not applied on 2026-11-27): rearm_ready delay computed from the pack voltage with a floor of 3.5 s or a SET_CAP tap; a REARM_REFUSED event with reason; emulator threshold 9 V. Second finding (N2): a 4-9 ms REARM tap latches the hardware (K1 operate at most 4 ms, U_HOLD turn-on at most 3 ms, both UNVERIFIED) but the firmware samples the set contact only every 10 ms or more, so it declares a fatal LATCH_NO_REARM in 7 of 10 phases at 4 ms (2 of 10 at 9 ms, 0 at 11 ms; simulated); requested: a fixed one-shot or a 20 ms minimum-press filter in hardware, 1 kHz sampling, and a refused set that drops the permit for 50 ms without a fatal fault. Both findings are fail-safe but invite workarounds. Evidence class: calculated and simulated.
